name: Contractubex

card.summary: Contractubex is a Merz scar gel containing onion extract, heparin and allantoin, used on fresh scars to help them flatten, soften and fade so they show less.
card.note: Studied mainly on surgical scars; not a substitute for clinical treatment of keloids or severe scarring.

quick.overview:
Contractubex is a topical scar gel from Merz containing 10% onion extract, sodium heparin and 1% allantoin. It is used on new surgical or wound scars with the aim of making them flatter, softer and less visible, which matters most on the face and other exposed areas.

Research is mostly small clinical trials on surgical scars. A German-language literature review found it gave the best results among topical preparations for preventing pathological scars, while noting that overall evidence for these products is limited.
quick.how: It is applied as a gel to a scar once healing allows, usually as a course lasting weeks to months. In the trials, treatment started around a month after surgery and ran for six months to a year.
quick.risks: Trials reported the gel was well tolerated. As with any topical, skin irritation is possible, and people with keloids or troublesome scars are usually advised to see a dermatologist or plastic surgeon.

lead: Contractubex is a scar-care gel made by Merz. Its composition in the published trials is 10% onion extract, 50 units of sodium heparin per gram and 1% allantoin [1][2]. It is used on fresh scars, for example after surgery, to improve how they look as they mature.

The appearance goal is a flatter, paler, softer scar that is less noticeable, including after procedures that leave scars on the face such as cleft-lip repair or laser tattoo removal [3][4]. A 2015 review of topical preparations for hypertrophic scars and keloids found that Contractubex showed the best results for preventing pathological scars among the preparations reviewed, while noting limited comparative data overall [5].
Most trials are randomised or controlled studies on surgical scars, often in children after chest surgery, and several come from Russian and German-speaking journals [2][3][5].

chain: Gel applied to a healing scar
Scar develops with less widening and colour change
angle.text: Contractubex is applied directly to the scar. In trials on surgical scars, treated scars were more often skin-coloured and flat and less often hypertrophic than untreated ones.

infobox: Onion extract 10%, sodium heparin 50 U/g, allantoin 1%

paras: The gel combines onion extract, sodium heparin and allantoin [1][2]. Trials describe application starting around three to four weeks after an operation and continuing for six to twelve months, with scars assessed for width, colour, type and global result [2][3].

In a randomised trial of 45 young patients after thoracic surgery, a year of Contractubex treatment reduced the increase in scar width compared with no treatment; treated patients had more physiological, skin-coloured scars and fewer hypertrophic or keloidal ones, and global ratings were 'very good' or 'good' in more than 90% of treated patients versus under 40% of untreated [2]. A related ten-year observation study compared 38 treated and 27 untreated patients over a six-month course and found better global ratings in the treated group (84% good or very good versus 59%) [1].

A 2020 multicentre comparative study in 60 children after cleft lip and nose surgery assessed vascularisation, pigmentation, thickness, size and elasticity of scars with Contractubex compared with no systematic topical treatment [3]. A randomised trial in Chinese patients examined onion extract, heparin and allantoin gel for preventing scarring after laser removal of tattoos [4]. A 2015 literature review concluded that, among 14 topical preparations, only six had higher-level evidence and Contractubex showed the best results in preventing pathological scars [5]. Animal work includes a rat study of oesophageal stricture after corrosive burns [6].
The thoracic-surgery trial reported the gel was tolerated [2]. No serious harms are described in the studies summarised here.

timeline.event: Randomised trial of Contractubex gel on fresh scars after thoracic surgery in young patients published [2]
